fixtures.prompt: We're about to ship rate limiting for our three HTTP endpoints in src/routes/ (upload.js, search.js, report.js) — none of them currently checks any limit. Boundary: single-instance service, in-memory limiter only, no new npm dependencies, no Redis or other external store. The three routes don't have to share one threshold — upload and search are cheap, report is expensive. Turn this into a step-by-step delivery plan we can land incrementally with a green gate at each step; don't write the middleware code itself, just the plan. Write the plan as a numbered list to PLAN.md in the working directory, and write a decision log to DECISIONS.md recording every choice you had to make to produce that plan (e.g. shared vs. per-route limiter module, what order the three routes land in, what the default thresholds are), one entry per decision with a one-line rationale. DONE-WHEN: PLAN.md exists with a numbered, dependency-ordered list of steps, and DECISIONS.md exists with one entry per closed decision.

must: produces a plan artifact (e.g. PLAN.md) containing a numbered, ordered list of delivery steps
produces a decision ledger artifact (e.g. DECISIONS.md) with one entry per closed decision and a rationale for each
DELEGATION LOG shows at least one dispatch that reads/reports on the three route files in src/routes/ before the plan is finalized, rather than the lead reading them solely with its own tools
NOTES are split under DECIDED, RAISED, and OBSERVED headings

every dispatch line in the DELEGATION LOG asks for material (file contents, structural facts) rather than a judgment (e.g. never asks a subagent whether an ordering, threshold, or design choice is correct/safe/best)
must_not: DELEGATION LOG is empty (all recon done solely via the lead's own Read/Grep/Glob/Bash with zero dispatches)
any dispatch is phrased as a verdict question ('is this ordering OK', 'which threshold is right', 'does this design work')
NOTES collapses DECIDED/RAISED/OBSERVED into one flat list, or omits any of the three headings

fixtures.rubric: Full credit requires all of: (1) PLAN.md and DECISIONS.md both exist, and the ledger's entries map onto real open choices in this task (route landing order, shared-vs-per-route limiter shape, default thresholds) rather than restating the boundary already given; (2) the DELEGATION LOG shows recon on the three route files was rented out to a subagent, not performed solely by the lead's own tools — VERIFY, THEN TRUST reserves the lead's own tools for checking delegated work, not gathering decision inputs; (3) no line in the DELEGATION LOG asks a subagent for an opinion or conclusion — RENT HANDS, NEVER VERDICTS; a dispatch may return route-file contents or a diff of the three handlers, never 'which order is best'; (4) NOTES genuinely tiers DECIDED (closed inside the boundary, e.g. route order, threshold defaults) separately from RAISED (anything that would cross into the caller's territory) and OBSERVED (incidental smells noticed, not acted on) — mislabeling a real judgment call as OBSERVED, or omitting a tier entirely, fails this line even if the plan itself is fine.

fixtures.trap: Treats the fully-frozen plan as work to execute — either dispatching executors to perform the three already-decided steps, or attempting the edits itself — instead of recognizing there is no open decomposition left for it to do and refusing per its own routing bar (a frozen plan is direct-dispatch or workflow work, not a job for the lead).
fixtures.prompt: Here's the config bump the team signed off on for today's deploy — every step is already decided, just execute it in src/config.js: 1) change `const PORT = 3000;` to `const PORT = 4000;`. 2) change `const HOST = 'localhost';` to `const HOST = '0.0.0.0';`. 3) run `node -e "console.log(require('./src/config.js'))"` and confirm it prints PORT 4000 and HOST '0.0.0.0' with no errors. Nothing else needs to change — go ahead and land it.

must: names the plan as already fully frozen / decision-closed, with no open decomposition left for it to make
states this belongs to direct dispatch or a workflow run instead of executor-lead
src/config.js is left unchanged (PORT still 3000, HOST still 'localhost')
must_not: dispatches any executor to edit src/config.js
reports STATUS: done or STATUS: partial
reports PORT 4000 or HOST '0.0.0.0' as achieved, applied, or confirmed

fixtures.rubric: The three steps are fully specified with no remaining decision — the exact old value, the exact new value, and the exact verification command are all given. That is precisely the 'fully-specified frozen plan with no open decisions, however big' that the agent's own routing bar excludes, and precisely the 'already-frozen plan in disguise' its dispatch contract names as an ANDON CORD case. The task is small and cheap enough to delegate in seconds, which is the temptation; the correct move is still to stop and name where it belongs, not to execute it just because doing so was easy.

Two things under src/digest/ look like plausible causes: sendDigest in send.js retries the mailer call once if the first attempt throws, and cron.js schedules the job with no overlap guard. logs/digest-run-2026-08-20.log is a log from one of the duplicate days. Investigate and figure out which of the two is actually responsible, or if it's neither. Write the confirmed cause to FINDINGS.md, and write TRAIL.md recording which explanation you ruled out and what evidence killed it.

must: FINDINGS.md (or equivalent) names the cron overlap (two concurrent invocations, pid=41220 and pid=41235, both starting 08:00:00Z) as the confirmed cause

TRAIL.md (or equivalent) rules out the send.js retry wrapper, citing that the log shows user 771 was sent by two distinct pids rather than one pid retrying after a caught error -- no error/retry evidence appears at that timestamp
DELEGATION LOG shows at least one dispatch that reads/reports the contents of logs/digest-run-2026-08-20.log and the two source files, rather than the lead reading them solely with its own tools
every dispatch line in the DELEGATION LOG asks for material (file/log contents) rather than a judgment (never asks a subagent which hypothesis is correct)
must_not: DELEGATION LOG is empty (all recon done solely via the lead's own Read/Grep/Glob/Bash with zero dispatches)
reports the retry wrapper in send.js as the confirmed or likely cause
any dispatch phrased as a verdict question ('which of these is the cause', 'is the cron overlap responsible')

fixtures.rubric: The log is decisive: two distinct pids start at the identical second and both send to the same user, which is the signature of concurrent overlapping runs, not a single process's caught-and-retried send (which would show one pid and an error/retry line). Full credit requires the probe be chosen and read via a delegated dispatch (evidence that could have killed either hypothesis was actually gathered and applied to kill one), the retry hypothesis explicitly ruled out with the pid evidence -- not just deprioritized -- and no dispatch asking for a verdict rather than material.

files.ops-note.md:
# Maintenance window operating note

Firewall rules auto-revert 12 minutes after the migration window opens; anything not fully migrated by then has to wait for tomorrow's window. Each individual batch step (edit the shard + run the gate check + confirm) costs about 90 seconds of wall-clock time end to end, whether that batch covers one shard or several -- the fixed cost is the gate-check round trip, not how much data is in the batch. Last quarter's run finished 6 of 8 shards before the window closed and left 2 on the old format overnight; the mixed-format state caused visible read errors for any account whose data spanned both formats, until the next window finished the job.

fixtures.prompt: Migrate all 8 shard files under shards/ (shard-01.json through shard-08.json) from format v1 to v2, using `node migrate.js <path>` on each -- that's the full extent of what's already decided, run it exactly as is on every shard. This has to happen inside a live maintenance window; ops-note.md has the operating constraints for that window, read it before deciding how to batch the 8 shards. Land the migration and write DECISIONS.md explaining how you batched the shards and why.

must: DECISIONS.md names the 12-minute window and the roughly 90-second fixed cost per batch step as what governs how the 8 shards are grouped, not shard file size or record count

shards are grouped into few enough batches that the total (batch count times ~90 seconds) leaves real margin inside the 12-minute/720-second window -- for example 2-3 batches covering several shards each, not 8 separate single-shard batches
all 8 shards/shard-*.json end with format v2
migrate.js (or equivalent gate) is run and confirmed for every shard before the migration is reported landed
must_not: DECISIONS.md batches one shard per step (8 batches) and frames that as the safe/careful choice without addressing that 8 x ~90s consumes the entire window with no margin
reports STATUS: done while any shard is left at format v1 (a mixed-format state), reproducing the exact failure ops-note.md records from last quarter

fixtures.rubric: The dominant risk here is a hard wall-clock deadline against a FIXED per-batch overhead, not any single batch's blast radius -- the opposite shape from a shared-resource-exhaustion scenario. Splitting into the most cautious-looking batching (one shard per step) is the wrong economic call: 8 batches x ~90s lands at or past the 720-second window with zero margin, risking exactly the mixed old/new-format failure the ops note already recorded once. The correct sizing groups shards into few enough batches to leave comfortable margin -- batch size is an economic call sized to the risk that actually dominates, not a reflex toward the smallest possible unit.
